subject: Hosted API evaluation — quickstart, endpoints & rate limits
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Jamie Park <jamie.park@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Lena Ortiz <lena.ortiz@acmehealth.com>
Date: Tue, 16 Jun 2026 15:34:00 -0400
Subject: Hosted API evaluation — quickstart, endpoints & rate limits

Hi Jamie (and Lena),

Thanks again for taking the demo today — great discussion on your use cases for discharge summarization and triage routing. As promised, here’s a short follow-up with next steps to get you started on the Hosted API evaluation: 

1) Quickstart (30 min):
   - Create an API key in Console > API Keys.
   - Hit the /v1/chat/completions endpoint with your key (example curl below).
   - We recommend starting with model: redwood-llm-1-large and max_tokens: 512 for evaluation.

2) Endpoints: (hosted)
   - Base URL: https://api.redwood.com
   - Chat: POST /v1/chat/completions
   - Embeddings: POST /v1/embeddings

3) Rate limits & quotas (initial eval):
   - Default: 60 requests/minute per key, 4 concurrent streams.
   - Burst: short bursts up to 120 RPM for new signups; we can raise this for your pilot.

4) Data and compliance: Hosted API encrypts customer data at rest and in transit. If you need VPC or on-prem options for PHI, we can discuss Redwood Private (VPC/on-prem) and Dedicated capacity separately.

5) Next steps I propose:
   - You spin up a quick eval using the curl below and the attached quickstart PDF.
   - If your team expects sustained throughput > 200 requests/min or needs strict data isolation, we’ll schedule a capacity/architecture call with Aditya and Dev.

Sample curl (replace YOUR_KEY):

curl https://api.redwood.com/v1/chat/completions \n  -H "Authorization: Bearer YOUR_KEY" \n  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \n  -d '{"model":"redwood-llm-1-large","messages":[{"role":"system","content":"You are a helpful assistant."},{"role":"user","content":"Summarize this patient discharge note: ..."}],"max_tokens":512}'

Attachments: redwood-hosted-quickstart.pdf (quick start checklist and sample apps)

Let me know when you’ve run the quickstart and any early latency/cost observations — happy to jump on a follow-up next week.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com

From: Jamie Park <jamie.park@acmehealth.com>

Subject: Re: Hosted API evaluation — quickstart, endpoints & rate limits

Thanks Marissa — this is great and very clear. A couple of quick questions from our infra/security team: 

- For HIPAA/PHI, would hosted mean we are sending identifiable patient data to the Redwood-hosted environment? If so, what are our options short-term for evaluation (we have some de-identified test data but want to understand constraints).
- We expect peak pilot throughput around ~300 requests/min and bursts to 800 for short windows. Is Hosted able to handle that or would we need Dedicated capacity?
- Are there per-minute token limits or only request limits? We do a lot of long-context summaries (~2k tokens input).

If it helps, we can set up a short architecture call — Lena (cc) will coordinate times.

—Jamie
Director, Clinical AI
Acme Health
jamie.park@acmehealth.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Jamie Park <jamie.park@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev@redwood.com>, Lena Ortiz <lena.ortiz@acmehealth.com>
Date: Wed, 17 Jun 2026 11:05:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Hosted API evaluation — quickstart, endpoints & rate limits

Hi Jamie — great questions, summarized answers below and looping in Aditya (Solutions) and Dev (Security) to help with any technical deep-dive or SOC2/PHI specifics: 

- PHI on Hosted: Yes — Hosted API will process request payloads in our hosted environment. We encrypt in transit (TLS) and at rest; we offer contractual BAAs for HIPAA customers on Dedicated/Private contracts. For evaluation, using de-identified or synthetic data is the safest approach. If you need a BAA for evaluation, Dev can advise (we sometimes provide limited evaluation BAAs under MSA).

- Throughput (300 rpm typical, bursts to 800): Our standard Hosted tier has default rate limits of 60 RPM and 4 concurrent streams, but we can provision higher quotas for pilots — we typically recommend Redwood Dedicated for sustained >200 RPM with strict isolation. For short trials we can temporarily raise your hosted quota to 500–800 RPM depending on model selection and sequencing. Aditya — can you confirm capacity planning options and lead time?

- Token limits: We enforce model max context sizes rather than a global per-key token cap. redwood-llm-1-large supports up to 8k context. Per-minute token throttles are applied only in extreme abuse cases; normal usage is limited by requests/min and concurrency.

I attached a short text file with the current rate-limiting policy and quota request process. If you’re good, suggest we schedule a 45-min technical call (Aditya will lead) to review architecture, expected throughput, and any VPC/BAA requirements.

Proposed times: Thurs 6/18 10:00am ET or Fri 6/19 2:00pm ET — let me know what works and we’ll send a calendar invite.

Thanks,
Marissa

From: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>

Date: Thu, 18 Jun 2026 12:20:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Hosted API evaluation — quickstart, endpoints & rate limits

Hi Jamie — Aditya here. Quick follow-up with concrete options and next steps so you can pick what fits best: 

Option A — Hosted (fastest onboarding):
 - We can temporarily raise your hosted quota to 600 RPM and 10 concurrent streams for the pilot (24–72h provisioning).
 - Pros: no infra ops, fastest time-to-value.
 - Cons: data processed in our hosted env; for PHI we’ll need a BAA (available under contract) or you can use de-identified data for the eval.

Option B — Dedicated (reserved capacity):
 - Dedicated GPU pools provisioned for your tenant; sustained throughput of 400–2000 RPM depending on node count.
 - Pros: better isolation and predictability; can sign BAA.
 - Cons: procurement and lead time (typically 2–6 weeks) and commit costs.

Option C — Private (VPC / on-prem):
 - Private control plane with customer-managed networking or on-prem appliance for fully isolated PHI workloads.
 - Pros: full control, compliance.
 - Cons: longer lead time and integration effort.

Recommendation for pilot: Start with Hosted with increased quota for the first 2–4 weeks to validate latency/cost and model quality (we’ll set up monitoring and token/cost dashboards). If you hit steady sustained above ~200 RPM or require contractual BAAs immediately, move to Dedicated.

Next steps:
 - If you want the temporary hosted quota increase, approve and I’ll request quota change (we’ll need expected sustained RPM and peak burst windows).
 - Schedule a 45-min technical deep-dive — book here: https://calendly.com/aditya-redwood/tech-deep-dive or suggest a slot and I’ll send an invite.

Attached: rate-limits-and-quotas.txt

Happy to jump on the call — we’ll bring someone from infra if you want to test throughput.

Regards,
Aditya Rao
Solutions Engineer
